If we let $u=-2(x-1),$ then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\,⟹\,-\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=\,\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $1 + \ln{(4 )}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{1 + \ln{(4 )}}-5{e}^{-2(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =-5{\int }_{1}^{1 + \ln{(4 )}}{e}^{-2(x-1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5{\int }_{0}^{-2\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{e}^{u}(-\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{-2})}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{2}({e}^{u}){|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{-2})} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{-2})}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}({4}^{-2}-1) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}(\frac{1}{16}-1) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot (-\frac{15}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{75}{32}\end{aligned}
